title: Make flat-file storage and scheduling catalog-aware
description: Use the configured status catalog from the preceding core/config task throughout the flat-file provider. Create configured status directories; dynamically iterate them for load, migration, status moves, cleanup, and recovery residue validation; and prevent a task from being silently ignored when its stored status is absent from the active project configuration. Preserve legacy default-layout behavior exactly when no states are added. Implement generic, permissive configured-state transitions in UpdateTaskStatus and atomic status-plus-metadata updates as required by the provider interface: any configured destination is valid, including reopening terminal states, and destination lifecycle timestamps are normalized by catalog rules. Only done resolves dependency readiness. Keep todo and paused eligible for ready/next exactly as today; waiting, blocked, failed, and other non-selectable categories must never be automatically chosen. Add focused flat-file tests for custom directory persistence, moves, create/reopen timestamp behavior, dependency blocking after failure, scheduling exclusion, migration/recovery residues, and rejected stale configuration.

comments.author: codex-wtp-loop
comments.message: Inspected the claimed task and existing catalog-aware core changes. Flat-file storage still hard-codes the four legacy status directories and transition rules; implementing dynamic catalog iteration, stale-status detection, permissive configured transitions, and focused provider tests.

comments.author: codex-wtp-loop
comments.message: Implemented flat-file catalog awareness: configured directories are created and iterated for load/migration/moves/cleanup/residue recovery; unconfigured task-status directories are rejected; configured transitions are permissive with catalog lifecycle normalization while legacy transitions/layout remain unchanged; dependency readiness resolves only on done and scheduling remains todo/paused-only. Added focused custom persistence, lifecycle/reopen, failure dependency, scheduling, migration/recovery, and stale-config tests. Verification passes: go test -count=1 ./..., go vet ./..., git diff --check.
